target_customer: Medicaid health plans and health systems paying for doula-led maternity support, serving pregnant and postpartum Medicaid members at no cost to them
problem: Medicaid mothers face poor maternal outcomes and gaps in follow-up; Malama pairs doula-care navigators with a gestational diabetes app and insurer contracts.
business_model: B2B2C care services reimbursed by insurers and Medicaid managed care plans, plus grants
product_category: Doula-led maternal care and digital diabetes-in-pregnancy support

founders.name: Mika Eddy
prior_employers: UnitedHealthcare (Director of Clinical Product Innovation; the launch post says Optum)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; Alpine Investors lists her in its 2022 Alpine Social Ventures fellow class.

founders.name: Daniela Bahamon Arango
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, which says she has 10+ years designing products for women; not described as an active founder elsewhere.

founders.name: Shalmali Bane
education: Stanford, PhD in reproductive and perinatal epidemiology (pursuing)
founders.background_notes: Listed in the launch post; per YC page not among active founders.

competitors.name: Mahmee
competitors.what: Maternal health startup with insurer and health system integration
competitors.funding_then: USD 9.2M Series A led by Goldman Sachs Asset Management, May 12, 2022; USD 3M seed in 2019

competitors.name: Maven Clinic
competitors.what: Virtual clinic for women and family health sold to employers
competitors.traction_then: Reached unicorn status in 2021 per later coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: A diabetes-in-pregnancy tracking app is standard mobile engineering; the harder parts are clinical operations, payer contracting and outcomes evidence.

defensibility.rationale: In-network contracts with Medicaid plans and published outcome data take time to replicate, though doula services themselves are not proprietary.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought Malama in the sources reviewed; funded rivals focused on employer or commercial markets.

market_need_then: The founders' project began at a Stanford biodesign course around gestational diabetes; the company cites poor outcomes among Medicaid mothers and the launch post for a diabetes-in-pregnancy app described real patient need.

branding.domain_note: Uses heymalama.co, a prefixed domain on a .co TLD; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline That's Always There; the line Mothers hold the world together, Malama holds you

branding.brand_signature: Mothers hold the world together. Malama holds you.
branding.community_and_virality: Community baby showers in Solano County in 2025 and a Forbes quote on its site, per search results.

brand_strength.rationale: A meaningful Hawaiian word for caring and a consistent warm voice with Forbes and trade press; no evidence of the brand driving growth beyond care partnerships.

pivots.to: Doula-led care navigation for Medicaid members plus the app
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC description now leads with doula-led support at no cost to patients

outcome_analysis: Malama began from a Stanford biodesign project on diabetes in pregnancy and grew into a Medicaid-first doula care model with about 35 staff, in-network contracts and a randomized trial result. It was slow to raise institutional money: the first sizable priced round found is a 9.2M seed in March 2026, after a 2.4M NIH grant in 2025. It is active and growing but remains early stage.
notes: The 9.2M seed is stated by HIT Consultant and Pulse 2.0; aggregators list 6.9M and 92.0M (a typo) and are ignored. The seed includes a 2.3M NIH grant and over 1M in California funding per HIT Consultant, so the pure equity portion is less than 9.2M and the amount is as reported. The YC page reports a 2.4M NIH Fast Track SBIR in September 2025 while HIT Consultant says 2.3M; both recorded as reported. Pre-seed amount not disclosed. Fierce Healthcare returned 403 and was not read. Malama is Hawaiian for to care for per dictionary sources, but no company source states that as the origin, so name_origin is null. Founders Bahamon Arango and Bane are on the launch post per the YC page; the company site names none.
